This image shows a gross pathology specimen, which is a piece of tissue that has been surgically removed from a body. It is not a photograph of a whole person, so an "abdomen" as a complete anatomical region is not present in the image.

The specimen itself consists of a large, yellowish, lobulated mass that appears to be composed of fatty (adipose) tissue. A mass with this appearance could represent several things, such as a large lipoma (a benign fatty tumor) or other types of fatty growth.

For an accurate identification and diagnosis, this specimen must be examined by a qualified pathologist. Please consult a medical professional for the interpretation of medical images or for any health-related concerns.
